chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Sullivan's five-piece dixieland band at a Danville dance school
summary: He joined drummer Sullivan's faking band of drums, piano, clarinet, trombone and trumpet; the dance school paid well until the owner vanished in the last week.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: And I think I went from there to -- I went to -- oh, I carried my wife home to see my mother. I went to Arkansas to see my mother. And then, while I was down there, I got a letter from Sullivan to join him with a band in Danville, Virginia.
Who was Sullivan?
Sullivan was a little drummer. That's all I know. He played drums. And it was a small combination -- drums, piano, clarinet, trombone and trumpet. Five pieces.
Sort of like a New Orleans style band.
Yes, and we played dances then.
Was it a fake band, or did you have a library?
No, we didn't have a library, we just -- that's what we did, just faked it. We called it the Green
Book. We just looked out of the Green Book. You had a number, 'why don't you play so and so', we just started to play it. (unintelligible)
Yeah. Was it sort of like the New Orleans bands, you know, that we hear from records --
Yeah, something like --
-- with cornet on top and the trombone on --
-- yeah, more like a dixieland, if I can think back.
Well, by this time I guess the Original Dixieland Jazz Band records were out.
Yes.
They were out in 1917, so --
Yes, because this little clarinet fellow we had, he was running all -- he was playing kind of obbligato runs all through the music, you know, while we were playing.
Uh-huh. Like the dixieland bands do.
That's right.
Did you think of it as being jazz or ragtime or just music?
Well, I have to think of it as being more a dixieland -- more dixieland than jazz. Yes.
And this was in Danville, Virginia?
Beg pardon?
HEMLOCK ERASABLE COTTON CONTENT
This was in Danville, Virginia?

Yes, this was in Danville, Virginia. Because, then we played there for a while. See, we were playing -- this was something of a -- he called it a dance school and stir them they were just that thick, you couldn't stand with a stick --
Yeah, dime a dance --
-- and they paid off well until the last week. Then the last week --
Uh-huh, then you get stuck.
-- the man -- we didn't know we played that week and the band was gone.
Uh-huh.
